description: Alianza Medio Ambientas, protejemos lo que amamos
summary: AGROCONECTA It is a mobile decision-support tool that primarily helps farmers in Cajamarca choose native crop rotations that are more resilient to climate change. It combines NASA Earth observations—such as soil moisture, precipitation, temperature, vegetation, and groundwater—with local soil data, crop characteristics, and the farmer’s own priorities (e.g., saving water, improving soil health, reducing risk, or maximizing income). Based on this, it simulates and compares various rotation scenarios and recommends the sequence of crops that best protects the soil, conserves water, and adapts to changing conditions.
details:
1. Detailed Project Description

1.1 What does AgroConecta do?

AgroConecta transforms complex spatial telemetry into practical growing-season decisions directly on the producer's Android phone, without replacing their local knowledge but complementing it with verifiable scientific evidence:

•     Historical and current environmental diagnosis: Analyzes 20 years of precipitation, mean/minimum temperature, and torrential-rain days (>= 12 mm) from NASA POWER, together with the Open-Meteo weekly forecast, to anticipate radiative frosts and water deficit.

•     Topographic and soil reading by polygon: When the farmer marks vertices on the Android map, the backend calculates exact area in hectares, elevation, mean slope, intra-plot elevation difference, and slope orientation (aspect) from SRTM 30 m.

•     Simultaneous comparison of three 24-month strategies: Evaluates the Baseline (the farmer's current practice) against a Water Resilience strategy and a Mixed Regenerative strategy across four Cajamarca seasonal windows.

•     Real farm-gate economics and responsible plant health: Cross-checks costs and revenues for 24 Andean crops (14 with an official live quotation converted to farm-gate price and 10 using INIA technical reference) and delivers integrated management guides with SENASA pre-harvest intervals.

•     Interactive in-field visualization and voice assistance: Provides a clean satellite viewer with toggleable NASA GIBS layers, a 24-month agronomic calendar, a native SVG radar chart, a climate simulator, and a conversational copilot in Spanish and Quechua.

1.2 How it works: key technical innovations

•     1. Multiscale Biophysical Harmonizer (biophysical_harmonizer.py): Integrates four physical pillars — Climate (T2M, Tmin, anomalies, and POWER storms), Water (precipitation, P - ET0 water balance, ERA5-Land/GWETTOP moisture, and drought stress), Vegetation (Sentinel-2 NDVI at 10 m with SCL cloud mask), and Soil (SoilGrids + field adjustment) — applying adiabatic downscaling (-0.0065 °C/m from the MERRA-2/POWER grid to the SRTM elevation) and thermal-inversion correction on flat terrain (slope < 5.5% between 2,000 and 2,850 m). It also explicitly declares which layers operate at 10 m, 30 m, 250 m, ~9 km, or ~50 km.

•     2. 5-Axis MCDA Multi-Criteria Engine with Non-Linear Contrast (scoring.py): Evaluates five components normalized from 0 to 100: Water Conservation (water_conservation), Soil Fertility and Nitrogen (soil_fertility), Erosion Control (erosion_control), Pest Cycle Break (pest_break), and Commercial/Forage Value (commercial_forage). The farmer's five priorities are weighted using a normalized power contrast w_i^2.5 so that their main concern makes a real difference in the ranking.

•     3. Satellite + Polygon + Farmer Reality Integration (parcel_service.py): Combines SoilGrids ISRIC v2.0 (with automatic probing of an agricultural ring of ~450 m when a peri-urban pixel is masked) with seven variables declared in the field: perceived texture, acidity, waterlogging or compaction, local early frost, seven water-availability modes (rainfed to drip irrigation), tillage type (ox-team/manual, rented tractor, or mechanized), and production purpose (self-consumption/market, dairy cattle/forage, or commercial grain).

•     4. Agronomic Engine and Real Farm-Gate Economic Conversion (rotation_engine.py and market_prices_client.py): Considers Pulgar Vidal ecological zones (from Yunga Fluvial < 1,000 m to Jalca >= 3,400 m), root depth, water requirement, symbiotic nitrogen contribution, anti-erosion cover, seeds available as indicated by the user, and net margins calculated with daily MIDAGRI/EMMSA prices converted from wholesale/FOB to farm-gate.

•     5. Structured Comparison of Three 24-Month Scenarios: Pits three homogeneous alternatives against the same real seasonal window: Strategy 1 (Baseline or current continuity), Strategy 2 (Water Resilience and Soil Protection), and Strategy 3 (Soil Regeneration and Mixed Profitability), accompanied by four explainable blocks (Rationale, NASA Evidence, Quantified Benefits, and Human-in-the-Loop Gaps).

•     6. Clean Satellite Viewer and NASA GIBS WMTS Layers on Android (leafletTemplate.ts): The mobile map starts on a clean base satellite image so the plot can be traced precisely, and lets the user turn on, switch, or turn off NASA GIBS WMTS layers (MODIS_Terra_NDVI_8Day, SMAP_L4_Analyzed_Surface_Soil_Moisture, IMERG_Precipitation_Rate) alongside OpenTopoMap topography and telemetry cards stamped Live / Saved / Estimated.

•     7. Bilingual Accessibility and AI Voice Copilot (VoiceCopilotModal.tsx and gemini_client.py): The entire mobile experience offers Spanish–Quechua translation (translations.ts), automatic voice reading (expo-speech), and conversational interaction by text or audio (expo-audio), directly synchronizing the map and the agronomic checklist without requiring advanced technical literacy.

2. Benefits and Objectives

AgroConecta converts global satellite series and scattered agricultural prices into concrete recommendations to raise the ecological resilience and net income per hectare of Cajamarca farmers:

•     Physical and chemical recovery of hillsides: Replaces the months of bare fallow after harvest with living covers (Oats + Vetch or Ryegrass + Clover) and nitrogen-fixing legumes (Tarwi, Fava bean, Pea, Lentil), reversing negative nitrogen balances into surpluses of +154 to +224 kg/ha in 24 months.

•     Drastic reduction of erosion and drought losses: In the evaluated plots, it reduces the physical erosion risk index by up to 75%–80% and lowers average water demand by 14% to 48% compared with traditional monoculture.

•     Economic transparency and prevention of over-indebtedness: Shows estimated seed investment, total season cost, benefit/cost ratio (B/C), and net margin in soles per hectare using verified official regional market prices.

•     Linguistic inclusion and documentary support: Removes technological barriers by offering Cajamarca Quechua translation, step-by-step spoken interaction, and a strict separation between live satellite measurements, cached data, and INIA reference estimates.

3. Presentation of Agricultural Analysis Results

3.1 Representative Case Study in Cajamarca

To validate the overall functioning of the system across contrasting production realities in Cajamarca, we evaluated three Beacon Plots calibrated with cached NASA POWER historical series (2006–2025), SRTM topography, and the official market prices captured on 11/11/2026 (BCRP exchange rate S/ 3.407/US$ as of Nov 12, 2026):

•     1) La Encañada / Combayo (3,360 m a.s.l. · Slope 15.0% · Strictly rainfed): Baseline of continuous potato monoculture on a steep slope, exposed to erosive rains and an estimated 47 cold nights per year, with high plant-health risk and loss of fertility (-202 kg N/ha).

•     2) Baños del Inca / Llacanora (2,675 m a.s.l. · Valley 2.2% · Gravity irrigation): Traditional potato–corn sequence with bare fallow in the dry season and an annual water deficit of -786.7 mm P-ET0 under winter thermal inversion in the valley.

•     3) Namora / Matara (2,845 m a.s.l. · Moderate slope 6.6% · Rainfed): Short potato–corn rotation with pronounced dry spells and potential for legumes and Andean grains with low seed cost.

4. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Models

AgroConecta strictly separates reproducible biophysical logic from the conversational artificial intelligence layer, avoiding black boxes and ensuring traceable answers even with intermittent rural connectivity:

•     Multimodal Audio and Natural Language Understanding (Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite): The gemini_client.py module receives text or base64-encoded audio turns (m4a/wav/mp3 via /api/voice-audio), performs automatic transcription, and uses responseJsonSchema to extract the farmer's intent (out_of_scope, app_help, parcel_qa, or rotation_planning) together with coordinates, irrigation, current crop, tillage, objective, and available seeds.

•     Hybrid Offline Deterministic Fallback Machine (voice_dialogue.py): When there is no access to the external API or the network fails in the field, a deterministic 6-slot engine with a Peruvian botanical dictionary (_PERU_CROP_ALIASES) and 22 calibrated localities takes over without interrupting the recommendation.

•     Adaptive Multi-Criteria Weighting and Suitability Modeling: The MCDA engine dynamically adjusts weights according to the farmer's priorities (w_i^2.5) and cross-checks thermal, water, and altitude requirements per crop (_crop_climate_fit) against the real polygon geometry.

•     Deterministic Detection of Climate Anomalies and Bare Soil: Identifies critical months of soil drought (soil-moisture z-score <= -0.75), monthly radiative frost risk (Tmin <= 2.2 °C), erosive torrential rains (>= 12 mm/day and 97th percentile), and vulnerability windows (NDVI < 0.25).

•     Explainable Recommendation System (4 Blocks): No score is delivered in isolation: each strategy automatically generates plain-language explanations of why it won, what spatial evidence supports it, how much it improves water/soil/margin, and which local observations the farmer needs to confirm.

5. Agricultural Forecast and Scenario Assessment

5.1 Historical Series 2006–2025, 2026–2027 Sensitivity, and Weekly Forecast

AgroConecta organizes the climate analysis into three clearly delimited and statistically honest time windows: (a) a real operational 7-day forecast (Open-Meteo Forecast) for immediate frost and rain alerts; (b) the observed 20-year historical series (2006–2025) from NASA POWER with ENSO modulation — which in La Encañada (3,360 m) shows a trend of +0.28 °C/decade, -3.0% rainfall/decade, and +14.9%/decade in storm events >= 12 mm —; and (c) short-term linear sensitivity (2026–2027), accompanied by the explicit notice (method_disclaimer) that it does not replace global CMIP6 climate ensembles.

5.2 Interactive Climate Simulator and Comparative Scenarios

To study how the strategies behave in drier or colder seasons, the interactive simulator ('What if...?') recalculates evapotranspiration (+4.5% for each +1 °C), soil moisture, erosion, and frost risk month by month, complementing the three 24-month rotation scenarios (Continuity E1, Water Resilience E2, and Mixed Regeneration E3):

6. Recommendations and Vision: Agriculture Based on Scientific Evidence

AgroConecta's technical proposal connects NASA Earth observation with everyday field practices under six action guidelines:

•     Continuous multiscale environmental monitoring: Combine clean plot views with Sentinel-2 time series, NASA POWER, and the 7-day forecast, keeping explicit traceability of each layer's spatial resolution.

•     Eradicate months of bare soil on slopes: Introduce cover crops and associated forages between main growing seasons to reduce topsoil erosion losses by 65%–80% on slopes > 15%.

•     Water savings adjusted to real availability: Adjust species selection to the real water regime (strictly rainfed, micro-reservoirs/qochas, or technified irrigation), avoiding high-consumption recommendations in areas with chronic deficit.

•     Biological recovery and responsible plant-health control: Prioritize symbiotic nitrogen fixation with Andean legumes, botanical rotation to break potato pest cycles, and strict compliance with SENASA pre-harvest intervals.

•     Accessible science and local language: Translate biophysical indicators into plain Spanish, Cajamarca Quechua, and understandable audio to close the technology adoption gap.

•     Participatory validation with specialists and the territory: Validate soil and yield recommendations together with the farmer in the plot, INIA Baños del Inca, SENASA, irrigation boards, and local universities.

8. Strategic Roadmap for Expanding Artificial Intelligence

Building on the operational foundation already implemented, the evolution of AgroConecta includes five priority technical lines in Phase 2:

•     Long-term climate projections with NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 (2030–2050): Replace short-term linear sensitivity with multi-model CMIP6 ensembles statistically downscaled to the Andean scale.

•     Expansion of NASA sensors (GRACE/GRACE-FO, thermal Landsat, and regional AppEEARS cache): Integrate groundwater storage anomalies (GRACE-FO), Landsat evapotranspiration at 30–100 m, and periodic ECOSTRESS/SMAP pre-download for the whole region.

•     Physics-informed models (PINNs) for frost in micro-valleys: Train hybrid networks on the SRTM 30 m grid to model nocturnal thermal inversion without requiring a physical weather station in every hamlet.

•     Graph networks (GNNs) for plant-disease spread and computer vision on Android: Alert on early outbreaks of late blight (Phytophthora infestans) and coffee leaf rust between neighboring plots, and estimate leaf symptoms/soil texture from the phone camera.

•     Adaptive learning from field feedback and IoT sensors: Automatically recalibrate local yields, MCDA weights, and irrigation depths from harvests reported by farmers and community probes.

10. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

A clear distinction is made between the AI executed in real time within the product and the tools used in engineering and documentation:

•     1) Operational AI integrated in the platform (Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite in backend/infrastructure/gemini_client.py): Performs audio recognition on the farmer's voice notes (/api/voice-audio), JSON Schema-guided semantic understanding (without inventing coordinates, prices, or scores), and natural-language drafting of explanations relying solely on the numerical context calculated by the backend.

•     2) Deterministic Contingency (backend/domain/voice_dialogue.py): Fully backs up data capture and navigation in Spanish or Quechua through rules and 6 agronomic slots when the phone works with limited connectivity.

•     3) Generative assistance in project development: Used as support for modularizing the FastAPI backend and TypeScript frontend, building automated economic and linguistic integration tests (subject to final validation with local speakers), and editorially structuring the technical documentation.

11. Expected Impact

AgroConecta demonstrates that NASA Earth observations, combined with detailed topography, transparent agronomic models, and daily prices from local markets, can become a practical tool in the small farmer's pocket. By replacing generic recommendations with 24-month sequences calibrated to each hillside, language, and farmer's budget, the project helps curb erosion and soil depletion in Cajamarca, reduce losses from frost or drought, and strengthen household income under a more resilient, evidence-based Andean agriculture.
